RE: Appeal of Adverse Benefit Determination
Reference Number: POC-7EB7CFD8B4-61417
Notice Date: 2026-08-20
Requested Service: Total shoulder replacement, CPT 23472
Treating Surgeon: Lindqvist, MD, Orthopedic Surgery

To the Appeals Committee:

I am writing to appeal the denial of prior authorization for a total shoulder replacement (CPT 23472), as communicated in your Notice of Adverse Benefit Determination dated 2026-08-20. The stated reason for denial was: "the clinical records submitted do not document an adequate trial of conservative treatment prior to the requested surgery." I dispute this determination on both factual and procedural grounds, explained below.

**1. The denial reason is not supported by the record.**

The clinical record that was submitted with the prior authorization request documents an extensive, well-documented, and unsuccessful course of conservative treatment for a 12-month history of progressive shoulder pain that has not been relieved by rest:

- Supervised physical therapy focused on range of motion and periscapular strengthening, completed over 8 weeks (2026-05-10 to 2026-07-05), totaling 16 visits, as documented in the physical therapy discharge note.
- NSAID therapy for 4 months with inadequate relief.
- A corticosteroid injection on 2026-05-11, which produced only 3 weeks of partial relief before symptoms returned.

In addition to this conservative-care trial, the record contains objective findings that corroborate the severity and irreversibility of the underlying pathology:

- Shoulder radiographs (true AP and axillary views) dated 2026-06-08 showing complete loss of glenohumeral joint space with osteophytes, subchondral sclerosis, and a flattened glenoid.
- CT imaging confirming an intact rotator cuff.
- Physical exam findings of glenohumeral crepitus, active forward elevation limited to 90 degrees, and external rotation limited to 10 degrees, with cuff strength intact.
- Functional loss including inability to reach overhead, inability to dress without assistance, and inability to sleep on the affected side.
- No active infection, no untreated substance use, BMI 29, non-smoker — no contraindications to surgery.

Given 12 months of symptoms, 8 weeks/16 visits of supervised physical therapy, 4 months of NSAID therapy, and a corticosteroid injection that failed to provide durable relief, combined with radiographic and CT evidence of end-stage glenohumeral joint disease, the medical record establishes both a completed conservative treatment trial and a clinical basis for surgery. I ask that the Appeals Committee review the complete file, including the physical therapy discharge note, imaging reports, and Dr. Lindqvist's clinical notes, and reverse the denial on this basis.

**2. I am requesting the specific medical policy or clinical criteria applied to this request.**

The denial notice cites only "the plan's applicable medical policy and clinical review criteria" without naming a specific policy title, number, or effective date. I am formally requesting, in writing and free of charge, the exact medical necessity criteria (including title, policy/guideline number, and version or effective date in force on the date of review) that were used to evaluate this request for CPT 23472, so that I and my surgeon can respond to the precise criteria rather than a general description. I have not been able to independently verify or obtain the full text of this criteria document, and I am not in a position to quote or agree to any specific criteria language until the plan provides it. Please include this document with your response to this appeal.

**3. Please clarify plan type and the applicable appeal deadline.**

The notice identifies my plan as "Highmark Health Options (Commercial/ACA)." Highmark Health Options' own published member materials describe it as a Delaware Medicaid managed-care and Medicare D-SNP plan, and Highmark's separately published Medicaid appeals procedure states that a member must file an appeal within 60 calendar days of the Notice of Adverse Benefit Determination — not the 180 days stated in my denial notice, which appears to correspond to Highmark's Commercial/ACA appeal timeframe. Because of this inconsistency, I am filing this appeal promptly and well within both the 60-day and 180-day windows, but I ask that Highmark Health Options confirm in writing (a) which plan type actually governs my coverage, and (b) which appeal deadline and appeal-rights framework (Medicaid vs. ACA/commercial) applies to this request, including my rights to a State Fair Hearing or external review, as applicable.

**Requested outcome:**

I ask that Highmark Health Options:
1. Reverse the denial of CPT 23472 (total shoulder replacement) and approve the requested prior authorization; or, in the alternative,
2. Provide the specific medical policy/clinical criteria applied to this determination, along with a clear explanation of exactly which documented element of conservative treatment or clinical finding was considered insufficient, so that any remaining deficiency can be addressed; and
3. Confirm my correct plan type and the appeal deadline and rights applicable to my coverage.

Enclosed with this appeal are copies of:
- Physical therapy discharge note (2026-05-10 to 2026-07-05)
- Corticosteroid injection record (2026-05-11)
- Shoulder radiograph report (2026-06-08)
- CT imaging report
- Dr. Lindqvist's clinical/exam notes
- [Any additional records the provider's office is submitting]

Please direct all correspondence regarding this appeal to me at the address and phone number above, or to my authorized representative, [representative name and contact information, if applicable]. I can be reached to provide any additional information needed to complete this review.

Sincerely,

Morgan Mercado
Member ID: W211915898
